title: Philosopher's Reactor
one_liner: Run a toy fusion plant whose mercury-lined walls make gold alongside electricity.
speaker: Peter Diamandis, Alex Wissner-Gross
context: A San Francisco fusion startup claims it turned mercury into stable gold, beating CERN's record. Its paper estimated about two tons of gold a year per gigawatt plant, and Alex framed this as the dawn of femtotech.
demo: Visitors see an animated neutron bombarding mercury nuclei that turn into gold, then scale up a plant with a gigawatt slider and watch a gold-bar counter fill year by year. They type in a gold price to see the gold revenue next to an electricity revenue they enter, and a 'gold bug' meter shows what happens to scarcity as more plants are added. A side panel tells the aluminum-utensils story as a historical parallel.
data_plan: Bundled figures from the podcast, with gold price and electricity value entered by the user. The nuclear animation is a labeled simplification.
risks: The company's claims aren't independently confirmed, and the two-tons figure is a paper estimate. Salim later says 'two and a half tons,' which conflicts with that estimate. Nothing in the demo should read as gold investment advice.
